file_insights.changes_made: Added cache_page decorator import and applied it to dashboard view
file_insights.significance: Performance optimization - caches dashboard view for 300 seconds

patterns_discovered.description: cache_page decorator placed before login_required decorator
patterns_discovered.context: Proper ordering of decorators - cache decorator applied first (outer), then authentication check (inner)

patterns_discovered.description: Dashboard view decorated with 300-second page cache
patterns_discovered.context: Identified dashboard as computationally expensive, warranting caching strategy

patterns_discovered.description: New import added to existing cache-related imports section
patterns_discovered.context: Maintained consistent import grouping with other django.views.decorators imports

gotchas_discovered.description: cache_page must be applied before authentication decorators to properly cache authenticated requests
gotchas_discovered.mitigation: Decorator correctly placed as outermost decorator in this implementation

gotchas_discovered.description: 300-second cache duration set without apparent cache busting mechanism for inventory updates
gotchas_discovered.note: May lead to stale data display until cache expires or is manually cleared

gotchas_discovered.description: cache_page caches per user session by default, but dashboard may contain user-agnostic inventory data
gotchas_discovered.mitigation: Review if different users see different dashboard data

approach_outcome.notes: Straightforward implementation achieved on first attempt with proper import and decorator placement

recommendations.details: Add signal handlers to clear dashboard cache when MaterialStock or related models are updated
Track cache performance to validate that 300-second TTL is optimal for usage patterns
Test that cached data persists for 300 seconds and cache is properly invalidated on inventory changes
Document why 300 seconds was chosen and any cache invalidation mechanisms in place
